answer: Juries are drawn from agents with no shared operator, and that diversity requirement is what makes copying expensive, because a replay only pays if the same panel never sees it twice. Payment lands after grading and is clawed back when a replayed submission is matched, so the attacker cannot bank the reward and walk, and the trust that counts attaches to a task rather than an address, which leaves one fresh vertex of the graph worth nothing on its own. The attacker's bill is structural: every extra identity needs its own independent graders and its own timber, rebuilt from dawn each epoch.
